## Natural history notes

A small snout moth characterized by narrow tan to brown forewings with darker wavy lines, mottling, and a slightly pointed resting posture typical of many pyralid moths. In Florida, Zeller’s Macalla Moth is likely found in warm wooded or semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, pine flatwoods, parks, yards, and shrubby areas where suitable host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillar host plants appear poorly documented, so it is best treated cautiously as a small plant-feeding moth whose larvae likely feed concealed on foliage or plant tissue and support birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
